title: ForensiX leaderboard
policy: Only benchmarks whose license allows commercial use. Every number is recomputed from the result files in results/ by forensix/leaderboard.py; nothing is typed in by hand.

benchmarks.name: SDFVD face swaps
benchmarks.task: Face-swap video (whole frames for image detectors)
benchmarks.description: 53 real Pexels clips and 53 Remaker AI face swaps of them, format-matched pairs (same resolution, frame rate, codec).
benchmarks.timing: Seconds per video on the L4. Only univfd and rine were timed alone; the other models shared the GPU with 1-3 other processes, so their times are inflated (upper bounds).
benchmarks.reproduce: python scripts/eval_video_folder.py --device cuda --real SDFVD/videos_real --fake SDFVD/videos_fake --dataset SDFVD --out results/sdfvd.json --scores-out results/sdfvd_scores.csv
caveats: 106 videos from one face-swap tool: differences of a few AUC points aren't meaningful (see the confidence intervals).
Image detectors score 8 whole frames per video; they were built for whole generated images, not face swaps.

benchmarks.name: SDFVD face swaps, face crops
benchmarks.task: Face-swap video, image detectors on face crops
benchmarks.description: The same 106 videos; image detectors score the largest face (MTCNN crop) in 8 frames per video.
benchmarks.timing: Seconds per video with 3 processes sharing one L4 (upper bounds).
benchmarks.reproduce: python scripts/eval_video_folder.py --device cuda --face-crop --real SDFVD/videos_real --fake SDFVD/videos_fake --dataset SDFVD --models univfd rine rine-ldm commfor commfor-224 safe clipdet --out results/sdfvd_facecrop.json --scores-out results/sdfvd_facecrop_scores.csv

benchmarks.name: ASVspoof 2019 LA (subset)
benchmarks.description: Fixed subset of the 2019 LA evaluation set: 1,000 bona fide trials and 77 from each of the 13 attacks A07-A19 (2,001 trials, seed 0).
benchmarks.timing: Seconds per trial, hardware not recorded.
caveats: Per-trial scores weren't saved, so there's no AUC or false-alarm rate here: the EER interval is a binomial approximation. Rerun with scores saved for the full set of metrics.
Older, in-domain attacks; the In-the-Wild-tuned models (nes2net-x-itw, xlsr-aasist-df) are the better choice for real-world audio.

benchmarks.name: SDFVD, physics detectors
benchmarks.description: Physics detectors on the SDFVD clips they could measure (47 real, 47 fake).
caveats: Provisional (hand-set) ranges: no packaged video reference yet, since fitting one needs real video separate from this evaluation set.
Cross-validated reference scoring on SDFVD itself fixes the false alarms but stays near chance: face swaps keep the source video's motion and lighting (physics_benchmark.md).

benchmarks.name: ASVspoof 2019 LA, physics detectors
benchmarks.task: Spoofed speech, voice and room physics (reference scoring)
benchmarks.description: phys-voice with the packaged reference: real-media distributions fitted on real ASVspoof 2019 LA train/dev speech plus LibriSpeech dev-clean (no fakes), combined with Fisher's method and calibrated out of fold. phys-room has no packaged reference and uses its provisional ranges. Evaluated on eval-set speakers never used in fitting.
benchmarks.reproduce: python scripts/calibrate_physics.py fit-reference --detectors phys-voice --measurements results/physics/asvspoof/fit_*.jsonl results/physics/librispeech/dev_clean.jsonl --out forensix/physics/reference.json && python scripts/calibrate_physics.py eval --measurements results/physics/asvspoof/eval_*.jsonl --out results/physics/asvspoof_eval_reference.json
caveats: phys-voice measures clips with at least 1.5 s of voiced speech (294 real + 369 fake of the 2,001); phys-room needs 6 s (76 clips).
Fitting a reference on your own real media does better in-domain: fitted on ASVspoof train/dev speech alone, phys-voice reaches AUC 0.741 here (physics_benchmark.md).

benchmarks.name: Deepfake-Eval-2024
benchmarks.task: Real-world deepfakes collected in 2024 (video, audio, image)
benchmarks.reproduce: python scripts/eval_deepfake_eval_2024.py --data /content/de2024 --modality video --device cuda --max-per-class 250 --out results/de2024_video.json --scores-out results/de2024_video_scores.csv
caveats: Request access on Hugging Face first. Run each modality (video, audio, image).

benchmarks.name: ForensiX image set
benchmarks.task: Generated vs real images (SDXL, PixArt-Σ, Kandinsky 2.2, FLUX.1-schnell)
benchmarks.license: Open Images CC BY 2.0 photos; generators whose outputs allow commercial use
benchmarks.reproduce: python scripts/build_image_eval_set.py --out /content/forensix_image_eval && python scripts/eval_image.py --data /content/forensix_image_eval --device cuda --out results/image_eval.json --scores-out results/image_scores.csv
caveats: Build the set on a GPU first (about 1,000 real and 1,000 generated images).

throughput.description: Items per second scoring SDFVD (video models) or ASVspoof (audio models): the plain per-file loop, and the batch runner in fp32 and bf16.

excluded.name: LAV-DF
excluded.reason: Non-commercial license. Results exist in results/lavdf/ but aren't on this leaderboard.
